title: Draft: WSML: XML Export of the dissection tree
description:
WSML (Wireshark Markup language) is an XML based format that is inteded
for exporting the dissection tree including essential information for
atomated processing like alls fields with their types, values and
representaions but also the related buffers.

notes.body:
Related to: #18993

Currently none of the export formats supported by Wireshark allow to export a "complete" dissection tree. This includes the buffers as well as the fields with some essential information such as the type of field. For this reason, I would like to suggest WSML as an additional export format that meets this requirement.

Here is a small example of what a WSML export could look like:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<wsml major_version="1" minor_version="0" tool="wireshark" tool_major_version="4" tool_minor_version="1" tool_patch_version="0" creation_time="1681814943" capture_file="D:\Dev\InspectorPacket\b.pcapng">
<packet number="5" length="12" captured_length="12" timestamp_seconds="1645094923" timestamp_nanoseconds="405333000" info="">
  <buffer>001964000FEFFE0</buffer>
  <field name="frame" display_name="Frame" type="FT_PROTOCOL" value="" start_position="0" length="12" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation="Frame 5: 12 bytes on wire (96 bits), 12 bytes captured (96 bits) on interface CAN-9, id 4">
    <field name="frame.section_number" display_name="Section number" type="FT_UINT32" value="1" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.interface_id" display_name="Interface id" type="FT_UINT32" value="4" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation="Interface id: 4 (CAN-9)">
      <field name="frame.interface_name" display_name="Interface name" type="FT_STRING" value="CAN-9" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    </field>
    <field name="frame.encap_type" display_name="Encapsulation type" type="FT_INT16" value="125" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.time" display_name="Arrival Time" type="FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME" value="Feb 17, 2022 11:48:43.405333000 Mitteleuropäische Zeit" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.offset_shift" display_name="Time shift for this packet" type="FT_RELATIVE_TIME" value="0.000000000" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.time_epoch" display_name="Epoch Time" type="FT_RELATIVE_TIME" value="1645094923.405333000" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.time_delta" display_name="Time delta from previous captured frame" type="FT_RELATIVE_TIME" value="-0.000163000" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.time_delta_displayed" display_name="Time delta from previous displayed frame" type="FT_RELATIVE_TIME" value="-0.000163000" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.time_relative" display_name="Time since reference or first frame" type="FT_RELATIVE_TIME" value="-1.674272000" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.number" display_name="Frame Number" type="FT_UINT32" value="5" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.len" display_name="Frame length on the wire" type="FT_UINT32" value="12" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation="Frame Length: 12 bytes (96 bits)"/>
    <field name="frame.cap_len" display_name="Frame length stored into the capture file" type="FT_UINT32" value="12" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation="Capture Length: 12 bytes (96 bits)"/>
    <field name="frame.marked" display_name="Frame is marked" type="FT_BOOLEAN" value="0" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.ignored" display_name="Frame is ignored" type="FT_BOOLEAN" value="0" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="frame.protocols" display_name="Protocols in frame" type="FT_STRING" value="can:data" start_position="0" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
  </field>
  <field name="can" display_name="Controller Area Network" type="FT_PROTOCOL" value="" start_position="0" length="12" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="true" representation="Controller Area Network, ID: 406 (0x196), Length: 4">
    <field name="can.id" display_name="ID" type="FT_UINT32" value="406" start_position="0" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="can.flags.xtd" display_name="Extended Flag" type="FT_BOOLEAN" value="0" start_position="0" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="can.flags.rtr" display_name="Remote Transmission Request Flag" type="FT_BOOLEAN" value="0" start_position="0" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="can.flags.err" display_name="Error Message Flag" type="FT_BOOLEAN" value="0" start_position="0" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
    <field name="can.len" display_name="Frame-Length" type="FT_UINT8" value="4" start_position="4" length="1" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="true" representation=""/>
    <field name="can.reserved" display_name="Reserved" type="FT_BYTES" value="00:00:00" start_position="5" length="3" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="true" representation=""/>
  </field>
  <field name="data" display_name="Data" type="FT_PROTOCOL" value="" start_position="8" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="false" representation="Data (4 bytes)">
    <field name="data.data" display_name="Data" type="FT_BYTES" value="fe:0f:fe:00" start_position="8" length="4" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="false" big_endian="true" representation=""/>
    <field name="data.len" display_name="Length" type="FT_INT32" value="4" start_position="8" length="0" buffer_index="0" hidden="false" generated="true" big_endian="false" representation=""/>
  </field>
</packet>
</wsml>
```

As an alternative to an XML-based format, one could consider whether it shouldn't be a JSON-based format?

I would be very grateful for extensive feedback and contributions to the discussion.

You mentioned including the type - is there any other information does this format/schema contains that was missing from PDML?
It also includes the buffers and the fields have a reference to the buffer (`buffer_index`). This becomes handy when you have reassembled buffers.
I also want add the `interface_id` of the frame to the `packet` tag. (Not done yet.)
